definitions.explanation: A large piece of cloth hung as a screen or divider, including stage curtains in theaters and decorative curtains used at events and ceremonies.

definitions.gloss: act (of a play or drama), scene
definitions.explanation: A division of a theatrical performance. Also used figuratively to describe a phase or chapter of events.

examples.japanese: {幕|まく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{上|あ}がった→上がる：00615_agaru⟧。
⟦{舞台|ぶたい}→舞台：03606_butai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{幕|まく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{下|お}りた。
examples.english: The stage curtain slowly came down.

examples.english: Red and white curtains were hung at the celebration.

⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦{戦争|せんそう}→戦争：01450_sensou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ようやく{幕|まく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下|お}りた。
examples.english: The long war finally came to an end.

examples.english: I feel the dawn of a new era.

notes:
USAGE:
Appears in many set expressions related to beginnings and endings. In kabuki and traditional theater, {幕|まく} is a fundamental structural unit. Also an important element in compounds related to the Edo period (⟦{幕府|ばくふ}→幕府：12448_bakufu⟧ = shogunate, ⟦{幕末|ばくまつ}→幕末：12531_bakumatsu⟧ = end of Edo period).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{幕|まく}が{上|あ}がる→幕が上がる：23975_makugaagaru⟧: the curtain rises (something begins)
- {幕|まく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{下|お}りる: the curtain falls (something ends)
- {幕|まく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧: to open the curtain (to start)
- ⟦{幕開|まくあ}け→幕開け：16042_makuake⟧: opening, beginning
- {幕|まく}{引|び}き: closing, wrapping up

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{幕府|ばくふ}→幕府：12448_bakufu⟧: shogunate
- ⟦{幕末|ばくまつ}→幕末：12531_bakumatsu⟧: end of the Edo period
- {幕内|まくうち}: top division (sumo); bento box
